news.title: Football: Soccer-Legacy key for 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup says sports executive
news.lede: CALGARY, Canada, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Focusing on ⁠the legacy of the Women's World Cup should be the top priority for those organising the 2031 and 2035 tournaments, according ⁠to a sports executive behind the 2023 competition. In Zurich on Monday, FIFA will confirm that the United States, Jamaica, Costa ‌Rica and Mexico will host in 2031, with England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland on co-hosting duties in 2035. Unlike Australia and New Zealand in 2023, there will be 48 teams rather than 32, streaming giant Netflix will have some involvement and the tournaments will be held in markets more mature in terms of women's soccer development than Australia. But ​for James Johnson, who was the CEO for Football Australia between 2020 and 2025 ⁠and is now the commissioner of the Canadian Premier ⁠League, legacy remains the fundamental driving force administrators should be thinking about.

news.title: Amputee World Cup: Dr Mohammed Raii delivers 30,000 bonus, promises further $120,000 if Black Challenge win trophy
news.lede: Ghanaian entrepreneur Dr Mohammed Raii has fulfilled his promise of US$2,000 to each member of the Black Challenge following their historic qualification for the final of the Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Raii, founder of the Eezzy Group Foundation, has also pledged a further US$8,000 to every player if Ghana beat Morocco to lift the trophy. The Black Challenge secured their place in the final after defeating defending champions Türkiye on penalties in the semi-finals, following an intense 1-1 draw after extra time. Raii said he wanted to make his commitment clear before the semi-final to avoid the uncertainty and disagreements that can sometimes follow sporting achievements, particularly over promised bonuses.

news.title: India face dilemma over Khalid Jamil's future ahead of 2030 World Cup qualifiers
news.lede: Bengaluru: With the next phase of the 2030 FIFA World Cup and Asia Cup qualifiers mere 10 months away, Indian football finds itself in a catch-22 situation over Khalid Jamil's future. . The question of whether to persist with the national team coach or make a change will confront the All India Football Federation after their polls next month. Neither option comes without considerable risk. . The decision to appoint Jamil was, in many ways, a financial compromise as well as a safe option for Kalyan Chaubey-led management.

news.title: Ghana vs Morocco: Why one Black Challenge star will miss Amputee World Cup final
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark YEN.com.gh as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Ghana midfielder Hamza Mohammed will be absent from the Black Challenge's first-ever Amputee Football World Cup final after the World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) Disciplinary Committee dismissed the country's appeal against his red card in the semi-final. The No. 8 was sent off shortly after Mohammed Mubarik netted from the penalty spot during extra time in Ghana's dramatic semi-final against defending champions Türkiye on Friday, 20 November. Ghana submitted an appeal in the hope of having the dismissal overturned in time for Sunday's final, but the disciplinary body upheld the decision, confirming that Mohammed will serve his suspension, according to Joy Sports.

news.title: What if Jürgen Klopp had coached Germany at the 2026 World Cup?
news.lede: There is an interesting question surrounding Germany’s 2026 World Cup campaign: What might have happened if Jürgen Klopp had been in charge from the beginning? Klopp had the opportunity to evaluate a large group of German players, experiment with different combinations, and establish a clearer picture of what he wanted from his national team. His approach offered an interesting glimpse into how Germany could have looked had he been given the job before the summer’s World Cup. One of the most revealing aspects of Klopp’s approach was his willingness to expand the player pool.

news.title: Drama surrounding 2030 World Cup broadcasting rights
news.lede: The battle for the future of sports broadcasting may be about to reach its biggest stage yet. FIFA’s upcoming sale of U.S. media rights for the 2030 World Cup is shaping up to be one of the most competitive auctions in sports history, with expectations that the package could command between $1.5 billion and $2 billion per The Guardian. What makes this auction especially significant is FIFA’s decision to bundle English and Spanish-language rights together for the first time. The move signals a preference for a single, exclusive rights holder and positions streaming giants such as Netflix, Amazon, Apple TV, YouTube, and DAZN as serious contenders against traditional broadcasters.
